     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	This rework plan addresses deferred items from the `2026-07-21-lcs-diff-pipeline` synthesis — adding ClassifyChanges isolation tests, fixing 21 locale-dependent test failures, cleaning up code inconsistencies, removing stale diagnostic simulation code, and optimizing O(n²) LINQ in Step 6b.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Replace the O(n²) nested LINQ pattern in Step 6b of `ClassifyChanges` (insertion attribution) with a two-pointer scan approach that achieves amortized linear time.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `Services/DiffService.cs` — Step 6b insertion attribution block (L434–477)
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- The nested LINQ pattern in Step 6b replaced with a two-pointer approach that pre-sorts `shiftedByRefPos` by `CurrentNumber`, maintains an index into the sorted list, and advances linearly across all insertions.
    19	- The `nextRemoved` lookup per insertion preserved (O(r) where r = removed count, acceptable for typical mod-list sizes).
    20	- The existing behavior preserved: each insertion at current position P attributes all unassigned shifted mods at current positions >= P up to the next removal boundary in reference space.
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- WP-003

    27	
    28	1. The Step 6b block in DiffService.cs no longer contains the .Where(s => !assignedShifted.Contains(s) && s.CurrentNumber >= inserted.CurrentNumber).OrderBy(s => s.CurrentNumber).FirstOrDefault() LINQ chain for finding the first affected shifted mod.
    29	2. The replacement code uses a two-pointer or index-advancing approach (a shiftedByCurPos list sorted by CurrentNumber with an advancing shiftedIdx pointer, or equivalent linear-scan mechanism).
    30	3. All existing tests (including the 10 ClassifyChanges isolation tests from WP-002, especially 9j: insertion with dependent-change attribution) continue to pass.
    31	4. The amortized time complexity for the insertion attribution loop is O(n) across all insertions when attribution ranges are disjoint, down from the previous O(n²) worst case of repeated full-list scans.

All localized text flows through the `LocalizationService` singleton, which detects the system culture at startup (`CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture`). The `ClassifyChanges` method has three minor code-quality issues identified during the original plan's review: an inconsistent null-`LineNumber` fallback strategy between Steps 1 and 3, a vacuous `.Where` filter in Step 6, and an O(n²) LINQ pattern in Step 6b.

    18	1. **Locale-aware test fixture** — Introduce a shared xUnit `IClassFixture<T>` that forces `LocalizationService.Instance.SetCulture("en-US")` before any test class that asserts on localized strings. 196	Add `using System.Diagnostics;` if not already present.
   197	
   198	**Step 12: Optimize Step 6b insertion attribution — replace O(n²) LINQ with two-pointer scan**
   199	
   200	In `Services/DiffService.cs` (L426–L461), replace the nested LINQ pattern with a two-pointer approach:
   201	
   202	Before each inserted entry is processed, maintain an index into `shiftedByRefPos` (pre-sorted by `CurrentNumber` for the lookup portion). For each insertion:
   203	1. Binary-search or linear-scan `shiftedByRefPos` (by `CurrentNumber`) to find the first unassigned entry at or after the insertion's `CurrentNumber`.
   204	2. Walk forward from that point, assigning entries until the next removal boundary or the end of the range.
   205	
   206	This reduces the amortized cost to O(k) total across all insertions when attribution ranges are disjoint (common case). Worst-case remains O(r × k) where r = insertedEntries count and all insertions share the same attribution range — acceptable for typical mod-list sizes.
   207	
   208	Implementation sketch:
   209	```csharp
   210	// Pre-sort shifted by CurrentNumber for insertion attribution
   211	var shiftedByCurPos = shiftedByRefPos
   212	    .OrderBy(s => s.CurrentNumber ?? int.MaxValue)
   213	    .ToList();
   214	
   215	int shiftedIdx = 0;
   216	foreach (var inserted in insertedEntries)
   217	{
   218	    int insertedCurPos = inserted.CurrentNumber!.Value;
   219	
   220	    // Advance past already-assigned or entries before this insertion
   221	    while (shiftedIdx < shiftedByCurPos.Count &&
   222	           (assignedShifted.Contains(shiftedByCurPos[shiftedIdx]) ||
   223	            shiftedByCurPos[shiftedIdx].CurrentNumber < insertedCurPos))
   224	    {
   225	        shiftedIdx++;
   226	    }
   227	
   228	    if (shiftedIdx >= shiftedByCurPos.Count)
   229	        break;
   230	
   231	    var firstAffected = shiftedByCurPos[shiftedIdx];
   232	    int startRefPos = firstAffected.ReferenceNumber!.Value;
   233	
   234	    // Next removal in reference space as upper boundary
   235	    var nextRemoved = removedEntries
   236	        .Where(r => r.ReferenceNumber >= startRefPos)
   237	        .OrderBy(r => r.ReferenceNumber)
   238	        .FirstOrDefault();
   239	    int? stopBefore = nextRemoved?.ReferenceNumber;
   240	
   241	    foreach (var shifted in shiftedByRefPos)
   242	    {
   243	        if (assignedShifted.Contains(shifted))
   244	            continue;
   245	
   246	        int refPos = shifted.ReferenceNumber!.Value;
   247	        if (refPos < startRefPos)
   248	            continue;
   249	        if (stopBefore.HasValue && refPos >= stopBefore.Value)
   250	            break;
   251	
   252	        inserted.DependentChanges.Add(shifted);
   253	        assignedShifted.Add(shifted);
   254	    }
   255	}
   256	```
   257	
   258	Note: The `nextRemoved` lookup per insertion is O(r) where r = removed count. For typical mod lists this is negligible. If removedEntries were also indexed by position, this could be O(log r), but that is not justified at current scale.
   259	
   260	### Section D: Diagnostic Cleanup
   261	
   262	**Step 13: Simplify `ReplacementDetectionDiagnostics.cs`**
   263	
   264	In `Tests/LoadOrderKeeper.Tests/ReplacementDetectionDiagnostics.cs`, remove the historical simulation section (approximately lines 100–230 — from the `GetModDiffAsync` call through the second-pass heuristic trace). Retain:
   265	- The class-level XML documentation (update to remove references to the simulation section).
   266	- The Arrange block (Scenario 16 test data setup).
